# Abbreviation expansions and the acronym stoplist. USER-EDITABLE.
#
# Feeds two things that must never diverge:
#   * acronym_variants() -- generating alias forms so "RAG", "Retrieval-
#     Augmented Generation" and "retrieval augmented gen" collapse to one id
#   * the Tier-1 grounding gate -- verifying that a parenthetical expansion
#     actually generates the acronym it claims

# Phrase -> alternative writings. The cross product with initial-compression is
# what produces RLHF from "Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback"
# automatically.
expansions:
  # ── core technique vocabulary ───────────────────────────────────
  "large language model": [llm]
  "artificial general intelligence": [agi]
  "artificial superintelligence": [asi]
  "reinforcement learning from human feedback": [rlhf]
  "reinforcement learning from ai feedback": [rlaif]
  "constitutional ai": [cai]
  "retrieval augmented generation": [rag]
  "chain of thought": [cot]
  "mixture of experts": [moe]
  "supervised fine-tuning": [sft]
  "direct preference optimization": [dpo]
  "proximal policy optimization": [ppo]
  "group relative policy optimization": [grpo]
  "vision-language model": [vlm]
  "generative pre-trained transformer": [gpt]
  # MCP collides with "master control program" and other non-AI uses; RAG
  # collides with the ordinary word "rag." Both need the surrounding-context
  # check in the grounding gate, not just the string match this file drives.
  "model context protocol": [mcp]
  "state of the art": [sota]

  # ── the thesis, spelled out ──────────────────────────────────────
  # Every lab names its own capability-scaling safety policy differently for
  # the same underlying concept -- without this collapse, RSP, "Preparedness
  # Framework" and "Frontier Safety Framework" read as three separate topics
  # instead of one desk (sweep_safety_alignment) covered by three labs.
  "responsible scaling policy": [rsp]
  "preparedness framework": [pf]
  "frontier safety framework": [fsf]
  # Same problem, three spellings, one concept: spending more compute at
  # answer time instead of only at training time.
  "test-time compute": [ttc]
  "inference-time scaling": [ttc]

  # ── benchmarks & evaluation ───────────────────────────────────────
  "massive multitask language understanding": [mmlu]
  "graduate-level google-proof q&a": [gpqa]
  "software engineering bench": [swe-bench, swebench]
  "abstraction and reasoning corpus": [arc-agi]

  # ── compute & infrastructure ──────────────────────────────────────
  "high bandwidth memory": [hbm]
  "tensor processing unit": [tpu]
  "application-specific integrated circuit": [asic]
  "chip-on-wafer-on-substrate": [cowos]
  "nvidia inference microservices": [nim]
  "floating-point operations per second": [flops, flop/s]

  # ── governance & evaluator bodies ─────────────────────────────────
  # CAIS (Center for AI Safety) and CAISI (Center for AI Standards and
  # Innovation, the renamed US AISI) differ by one letter and cover adjacent
  # ground; keep them as separate expansions rather than one fuzzy entry, or
  # the resolver will happily merge a safety advocacy nonprofit with a NIST
  # standards office.
  "center for ai safety": [cais]
  "center for ai standards and innovation": [caisi]
  "ai safety institute": [aisi]
  "ai security institute": [aisi]
  "national institute of standards and technology": [nist]
  "federal trade commission": [ftc]
  "cyberspace administration of china": [cac]
  "model evaluation and threat research": [metr]
  "machine intelligence research institute": [miri]
  "organisation for economic co-operation and development": [oecd]
  "fundamental ai research": [fair]
  "safe superintelligence": [ssi]

# Never treated as an acronym worth defining or matching. Either too common,
# too short, or universally understood.
stoplist:
  - US
  - USA
  - UK
  - EU
  - UN
  - CEO
  - CTO
  - CFO
  - COO
  - IT
  - PC
  - TV
  - OS
  - API
  - SDK
  - GPU
  - CPU
  - FAQ
  - PDF
  - URL
  - LLC
  - INC
  - LTD
  - IPO
  - VC
  # Generic computing term that happens to sit inside a product name
  # ("gpt-oss"); the model card itself notes the license isn't full open
  # source. Defining OSS on its own adds nothing this domain didn't already
  # know, and the product is tracked as its own entity regardless.
  - OSS
  # AI and ML: the two most common strings in this entire corpus. Defining
  # either as "an acronym found in the text" is circular -- the domain IS
  # artificial intelligence. AI survives below in short_whitelist, but only
  # for matching entity names that embed it, never as something to define.
  - AI
  - ML
  # Ticker symbols for organisations already tracked as entities under their
  # proper names -- stoplisted for the same reason RKLB would be in a
  # different domain: the company is already an entity, the ticker is not a
  # second one.
  - NVDA
  - MSFT
  - GOOGL
  - AAPL
  - AMZN
  - META
  - TSM

# Two-character acronyms that ARE meaningful here, so they survive the
# minimum-length rule. Everything else under 3 characters is dropped.
short_whitelist:
  - AI   # only as an entity alias (e.g. "Scale AI", "Mistral AI", "Runway
         # AI"), never as a definition -- see the stoplist entry above

# ── containment guard ────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Tokens that do NOT distinguish one organisation from another. `token_set_ratio`
# scores a token SUBSET as an exact match, so "DeepMind" hits "Google DeepMind"
# at 100 -- and that IS the same body. What separates a safe collapse from a
# wrong one is the extra tokens, and a containment match is accepted only when
# every extra token appears below. Anything else is filed in `alias_conflicts`
# for review.
#
# Add a token when two names are wrongly kept apart; remove one when two are
# wrongly merged.
non_distinguishing:
  # grammatical
  - of
  - the
  - and
  - for
  - in
  - on
  # corporate and legal form
  - inc
  - inc.
  - llc
  - ltd
  - limited
  - corp
  - corp.
  - corporation
  - company
  - co
  - holdings
  - group
  - platforms   # Meta's legal name is "Meta Platforms, Inc."; the word adds
                # nothing a reader would use to tell two AI orgs apart
  - pbc         # public benefit corporation -- Anthropic PBC, and the
                # structure several other labs are adopting; same role as
                # "Inc" or "LLC" above, not a name of anything
# Deliberately NOT here, and this is the inversion worth flagging explicitly:
#
# `united`, `states`, `us`, `uk`, `national`, `federal`, `american`, `china`,
# `chinese` -- safe filler in a domain with one country's armed forces, but
# this domain runs a whole international network of near-identically-named
# national bodies (UK AI Security Institute, the US CAISI, the broader
# International AI Safety Institute Network). Marking "UK" non-distinguishing
# would let "AI Safety Institute" containment-match every country's institute
# as the same body. That is the opposite of what happened with "United
# States Air Force" in a defense-flavored version of this file, where the
# jurisdiction word really was disposable.
#
# `labs` / `lab` -- disposable filler in domains where it names a generic
# government facility, but here it is frequently the load-bearing part of the
# name: "Thinking Machines Lab" and "Meta Superintelligence Labs" are not
# "Thinking Machines" and "Meta Superintelligence" with a word tacked on.
#
# `ai` -- the single riskiest omission in this file. It looks like corporate
# filler ("Scale" / "Scale AI") but just as often names a specific division
# distinct from its parent: "Google AI" is not "Google," "Meta AI" is not
# all of Meta. A missed merge here costs a confirmation click; a wrong one
# silently folds a subsidiary into its parent company.

# Tokens naming a company's legal or corporate FORM rather than a different
# company. Read only by the curation classifier, never by the resolver: the
# resolver must keep declining, minting and filing the pair, because a token
# added to `non_distinguishing` above makes it accept a fuzzy containment match
# silently -- writing an alias, taking the surface, filing nothing and showing
# nobody. What this list buys is that the filed pair is then classified as one
# thing spelled two ways instead of as a parent and a subsidiary, which is the
# difference between a decision the system can make and one that waits for you.
#
# `ai` and `labs` stay out for the reasons given above them: both are
# frequently the substantive part of the name, not a form of it.
corporate_form:
  - technologies   # Google DeepMind's own former legal name was "DeepMind
                    # Technologies Limited"; 1X Technologies is referred to
                    # as plain "1X" just as often
  - technology
  - global          # OpenAI's for-profit entity is "OpenAI Global, LLC" --
                    # same organisation, this is the subsidiary marker

# Head nouns a writer appends without naming a different thing. Counted ONLY
# when they trail the longer name, so "Stanford Institute for Human-Centered
# AI" keeps its Institute and only "Agentforce platform" loses its tail.
generic_tails:
  - platform
  - model
  - assistant
  - chatbot
  - app
  - tool
  - suite
  - family
  - project
  - initiative
  - report   # "AI Index Report" is routinely shortened to "AI Index" in
             # casual reference; the tail is the citation, not the name
# Deliberately NOT here:
#   `framework` -- "Preparedness Framework" and "Frontier Safety Framework"
#   are never shortened to "Preparedness" or "Frontier Safety" in the wild;
#   stripping it would produce a name nobody uses rather than a synonym.
#   `agent` -- too often names a specific product tier rather than a generic
#   descriptor (a hypothetical "X Agent" SKU distinct from base "X"); left
#   out on the same principle as everything else in this file that could
#   plausibly be part of a real name.
[structured-output-enforce] You MUST call the StructuredOutput tool to complete this request. Call this tool now.

structured_output.document:
# Abbreviation expansions and the acronym stoplist. USER-EDITABLE.
#
# Feeds two things that must never diverge:
#   * acronym_variants() -- generating alias forms so "RAG", "Retrieval-
#     Augmented Generation" and "retrieval augmented gen" collapse to one id
#   * the Tier-1 grounding gate -- verifying that a parenthetical expansion
#     actually generates the acronym it claims

# Phrase -> alternative writings. The cross product with initial-compression is
# what produces RLHF from "Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback"
# automatically.
expansions:
  # ── core technique vocabulary ───────────────────────────────────
  "large language model": [llm]
  "artificial general intelligence": [agi]
  "artificial superintelligence": [asi]
  "reinforcement learning from human feedback": [rlhf]
  "reinforcement learning from ai feedback": [rlaif]
  "constitutional ai": [cai]
  "retrieval augmented generation": [rag]
  "chain of thought": [cot]
  "mixture of experts": [moe]
  "supervised fine-tuning": [sft]
  "direct preference optimization": [dpo]
  "proximal policy optimization": [ppo]
  "group relative policy optimization": [grpo]
  "vision-language model": [vlm]
  "generative pre-trained transformer": [gpt]
  # MCP collides with "master control program" and other non-AI uses; RAG
  # collides with the ordinary word "rag." Both need the surrounding-context
  # check in the grounding gate, not just the string match this file drives.
  "model context protocol": [mcp]
  "state of the art": [sota]

  # ── the thesis, spelled out ──────────────────────────────────────
  # Every lab names its own capability-scaling safety policy differently for
  # the same underlying concept -- without this collapse, RSP, "Preparedness
  # Framework" and "Frontier Safety Framework" read as three separate topics
  # instead of one desk (sweep_safety_alignment) covered by three labs.
  "responsible scaling policy": [rsp]
  "preparedness framework": [pf]
  "frontier safety framework": [fsf]
  # Same problem, three spellings, one concept: spending more compute at
  # answer time instead of only at training time.
  "test-time compute": [ttc]
  "inference-time scaling": [ttc]

  # ── benchmarks & evaluation ───────────────────────────────────────
  "massive multitask language understanding": [mmlu]
  "graduate-level google-proof q&a": [gpqa]
  "software engineering bench": [swe-bench, swebench]
  "abstraction and reasoning corpus": [arc-agi]

  # ── compute & infrastructure ──────────────────────────────────────
  "high bandwidth memory": [hbm]
  "tensor processing unit": [tpu]
  "application-specific integrated circuit": [asic]
  "chip-on-wafer-on-substrate": [cowos]
  "nvidia inference microservices": [nim]
  "floating-point operations per second": [flops, flop/s]

  # ── governance & evaluator bodies ─────────────────────────────────
  # CAIS (Center for AI Safety) and CAISI (Center for AI Standards and
  # Innovation, the renamed US AISI) differ by one letter and cover adjacent
  # ground; keep them as separate expansions rather than one fuzzy entry, or
  # the resolver will happily merge a safety advocacy nonprofit with a NIST
  # standards office.
  "center for ai safety": [cais]
  "center for ai standards and innovation": [caisi]
  "ai safety institute": [aisi]
  "ai security institute": [aisi]
  "national institute of standards and technology": [nist]
  "federal trade commission": [ftc]
  "cyberspace administration of china": [cac]
  "model evaluation and threat research": [metr]
  "machine intelligence research institute": [miri]
  "organisation for economic co-operation and development": [oecd]
  "fundamental ai research": [fair]
  "safe superintelligence": [ssi]

# Never treated as an acronym worth defining or matching. Either too common,
# too short, or universally understood.
stoplist:
  - US
  - USA
  - UK
  - EU
  - UN
  - CEO
  - CTO
  - CFO
  - COO
  - IT
  - PC
  - TV
  - OS
  - API
  - SDK
  - GPU
  - CPU
  - FAQ
  - PDF
  - URL
  - LLC
  - INC
  - LTD
  - IPO
  - VC
  # Generic computing term that happens to sit inside a product name
  # ("gpt-oss"); the model card itself notes the license isn't full open
  # source. Defining OSS on its own adds nothing this domain didn't already
  # know, and the product is tracked as its own entity regardless.
  - OSS
  # AI and ML: the two most common strings in this entire corpus. Defining
  # either as "an acronym found in the text" is circular -- the domain IS
  # artificial intelligence. AI survives below in short_whitelist, but only
  # for matching entity names that embed it, never as something to define.
  - AI
  - ML
  # Ticker symbols for organisations already tracked as entities under their
  # proper names -- stoplisted for the same reason RKLB would be in a
  # different domain: the company is already an entity, the ticker is not a
  # second one.
  - NVDA
  - MSFT
  - GOOGL
  - AAPL
  - AMZN
  - META
  - TSM

# Two-character acronyms that ARE meaningful here, so they survive the
# minimum-length rule. Everything else under 3 characters is dropped.
short_whitelist:
  - AI   # only as an entity alias (e.g. "Scale AI", "Mistral AI", "Runway

  - for

  - on

  - llc
